title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-04-22
content:
Serving runtime weekly update — kernel + KV cache + batching
Date: 2026-04-22
Author: Asha Patel
Attendees: Asha, Liam, Rosa, Daniel, Priya, Marco (SRE)

Summary
- This week focused on three threads: (1) kernel selection and micro-ops for attention, (2) KV cache warmup and eviction policy improvements, and (3) dynamic batching heuristics for short-tail/interactive workloads.
- We deployed a beta kernel selector to the canary pool and observed measurable p50/p95 improvements on medium sequence workloads. KV cache hit-rate improvements are visible in internal perf dashboards after the new prefetch heuristics landed. Batching work continues: we landed a sliding-window batching prototype for groups of low-latency requests, but it needs tuning to avoid 95th percentile latency regressions during bursts.

Kernel work
- What we did:
  - Merged PR #482 (kernel selector) which adds runtime telemetry to pick between fused-attention and fallback kernels based on sequence length distribution and hardware occupancy.
  - Added micro-op scheduling to reduce kernel launch overhead for <64-token chains on A100 and H100.
  - Benchmarked across representative models: results show ~12% p50 improvement and ~8% p95 improvement for medium sequences (128-512 tokens) on H100.
- Metrics / Observations:
  - Canary pool (10% traffic): p50 down 12%, p95 down 8% vs baseline for neil-13B-opti.
  - Cold-start overhead for small batches reduced by ~30ms due to micro-op aggregation.
- Risks / Notes:
  - Some edge cases on older CUDA drivers (11.4) still prefer fallback kernels; added a driver-detection gate. QA to validate more driver combos next week.

KV cache and prefetching
- What we did:
  - Rolled out a modified prefetch policy to prioritize frequently re-requested prefixes (LRU-with-frequency) and tightened memory guardrails per-tenant.
  - Implemented an eviction-safety window to avoid evicting prefixes used by in-flight requests.
  - Added telemetry for per-tenant KV hit-rate and cold-request percent.
- Metrics:
  - Overall KV hit-rate improved from 72% -> 81% on the canary cohort for production traffic patterns (chat-style workloads).
  - Cold-request percent dropped from 18% -> 11% for the same cohort.
- Issues found:
  - One tenant experienced higher memory churn due to very long-running prefix chains; created ticket ENG-1242 for per-tenant TTL tuning and quota enforcement.

Batching (dynamic batching & sliding-window)
- What we did:
  - Deployed sliding-window batching prototype to a subset of low-latency routes. This groups short requests arriving within a 6–10ms window before dispatch.
  - Implemented adaptive max-window growth: window grows until p95 latency approaches SLO then backs off.
- Metrics:
  - Throughput improvement: token/sec increased ~9% for short-request-heavy routes when batching enabled.
  - Average latency: p50 improved slightly; p95 saw small regressions during multi-tenant bursts in one region.
- Action items:
  - Add per-route safety caps to prevent batching-induced queueing for premium SLO routes.
  - Add runtime telemetry for queue depth per-worker to detect harmful queue build-up quickly.

Standup / Meeting notes (syncs during week)
- Mon quick sync: kernel selector rollout schedule approved; canary to expand to 25% next Tuesday if metrics stay green.
- Wed deep-dive: SRE raised concerns about queue depth spikes when sliding-window growth is aggressive; decided to add backpressure thresholds.
- Thu postmortem prep: reviewed a 2-hour region degradation incident caused by a KV eviction bug; PR to patch went out same day.

Blockers / Open risks
- Driver compatibility on some older GPU hosts is causing fallback kernel regressions — need expanded QA and possibly a compatibility shim.
- One tenant with unusual prefix growth pattern requires per-tenant policy; blocking full rollout of aggressive prefetch.
- Batching p95 regressions under multi-tenant bursts need more granular throttles and per-route caps.

Decisions made
- Expand kernel selector canary to 25% on 2026-04-28 if no regressions.
- Hold full prefetch rollout until per-tenant quotas and TTLs for prefixes are in place (ENG-1242).
- Implement per-route batching caps for premium SLO routes before wider batching rollout.

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Liam: add driver compatibility test matrix and run on remaining host variants (ETA 2026-04-29).
- Rosa: implement per-tenant TTL/quota prototype and add to canary (ENG-1242) (ETA 2026-05-06).
- Daniel: add per-route batching caps and queue-depth telemetry (ETA 2026-04-30).
- Priya: expand canary telemetry dashboards to include per-tenant KV hit-rate and cold-request percent (ETA 2026-04-27).
- Asha: coordinate expansion of kernel-selector canary and prepare rollback playbook (ETA 2026-04-28).

Notes / Misc
- Marco (SRE) suggested a short runbook for detecting batching-induced regressions; will draft and share next week.
- Performance bench artifacts live in linked PR and Confluence page. Please add testcases you want on the compatibility matrix to the PR comments.

Next week plan
- Expand kernel selector canary (if green), continue driver QA, and iterate on micro-op scheduling.
- Ship per-tenant TTL/quota prototype to canary to unblock prefetch rollout.
- Harden batching: add safety caps, improve queue telemetry, and run multi-tenant burst tests.
